text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected for /streaming/generate — service: runtime-gw, region: us-west-2, window: 5m, p95=820ms, p99=2.4s :rotating_light:

alex: saw the alert. is this a global thing or specific to a pool?

maria: looks concentrated on the paging path for long-context requests. Most errors are streaming stalls + a big drop in prefix cache hit rate.

maria: p95 jump at ~1976002300, correlates with deployment of rollout/kv-prefixhash-v2 (canary).

alex: any customer impact?

cs-olga: Cx dashboard shows elevated error and latency for ~3 customers on dedicated pools — some request timeouts logged. I flagged CS tickets for two enterprise customers.

sre-raja: can we get the cache hit rate and ops logs?

maria: metrics: prefix_cache.hit_rate went from 92% -> 28% for prefix length 8 within the last 10m. KV read latencies spiked.

maria: logs (first pass):
```
[1976002356] runtime-gw: stream stall: shard=kv-26 prefix_hash=0x7a1a mismatch, cache_miss=true, backend_read_ms=1423
[1976002361] router: fallback to cold fetch, seq=...
[1976002370] runtime-node: emit stall_event, trace=abcd1234
```

alex: that matches a prefix-hash change causing low hit rate and more backend hits -> paging -> tail latency. good catch.

infra-jamie: rollout/kv-prefixhash-v2 was pushed at 1976002289 in canary (5% traffic) and then 30% at 1976002320.

alex: ok immediate mitigation options: 1) revert prefixhash rollout 2) enable aggressive prefix-cache-warmup 3) increase retry/backoff for streaming to hide backend tail. Which can we do fastest?

maria: revert is simplest and lowest risk. I can trigger rollback for the config and flush affected cache shards.

deploy-bot: Deployment event: rollout/kv-prefixhash-v2 -> rollback initiated by maria at 1976002451.

maria: running: `kubectl -n infra rollout undo config/kv-prefixhash-config --to-revision=1976002200` and then `curl -X POST https://ops-api/cache/flush?shard=kv-26` for hot shard.

sre-raja: I'll watch metrics and tail logs during rollback. alex, can you coordinate customer comms with olga?

alex: on it. olga, can you hold an update to the affected accounts: "We saw increased latency due to a cache key hashing rollout; engineering is rolling back and monitoring. Expect improvements within ~5-10m."

cs-olga: pinged customers. they appreciate quick response. one asked if this was due to model changes — confirmed it's infra config.

infra-jamie: flush triggered across 3 hot shards: kv-26, kv-11, kv-03.

maria: rollback succeeded on control plane at 1976002478. now flushing, then warming cache for common prefixes (script: `scripts/warm_prefixes --top=2000`).

maria: warming started. I see cache hit rate climbing: 28% -> 64% in the last 90s. p95 trending down.

sre-raja: p95 now 310ms, p99 760ms — moving toward normal. still watching streaming stalls count.

alex: do we need to enable any short-term fallback to the older paging/prefetch policy?

maria: already toggled router.fallback_preload=true for affected pools to reduce cold reads.

deploy-bot: Router config change applied by maria at 1976002522.

sre-raja: streaming stall events decreasing. tail latency spikes reduced.

alex: handing off to raja for the night. summary for handoff:
- root cause: prefix-hash rollout (rollout/kv-prefixhash-v2) reduced prefix cache hit rate due to hash distribution change -> more backend paging -> streaming stalls -> p99 SLO breach
- mitigation: rollback config to previous prefixhash revision, flush hot shards, warm top prefixes, enable router fallback_preload, monitored metrics until recovery
- customer impact: elevated latency/timeouts for small subset of enterprise customers; CS notified
- actions: create postmortem, include canary guard checks and improved metrics alerts for prefix_hit_rate delta > 20% in 5m

sre-raja: taking it. I'll keep the thread updated and open a postmortem ticket. thanks all.

lena_pm: note for postmortem: add release checklist item to require synthetic prefix-level canary tests before rollout beyond 5% traffic.

maria: digging into why v2 hash had skew — early hypothesis: seed change + missing normalization for non-utf8 keys. I'll open PR with test vectors.

alex: great. olga — let us know if customers escalate. otherwise we'll follow up with a timeline.

cs-olga: confirmed both affected accounts saw improvements within 8m of rollback. will keep them posted.

sre-raja: p95=210ms p99=350ms at 1976003005. Closing live mitigation. I'll file postmortem and assign to maria+jamie for follow-up.

oncall-bot: NOTE: incident triage created IN-1976002468, severity: sev2, owner: sre-raja.

alex: thanks team. we'll convert this to a postmortem thread in #postmortems — leave this for 1hr for logs then archive. :thumbsup:
